svg.title: Add CSV export to the reports page: arsenal feature delivery loop
svg.desc: A developer timeline showing research, planning, plan approval, worktree execution, independent verification, test gate, merge, and publishing. Continuous tracking runs in the right lane. Red arrows return findings to execution or planning; publishing seeds new research. S is strategist, E executor, R reviewer. Example choices are identified in the footer.
svg.text: One feature, from idea to release
Add CSV export to the reports page
Consumer application example · Six phases · Two hard gates · Three model tiers
S Strategist
E Executor
R Reviewer
Human Decisions / co-sign
DELIVERY TIMELINE
05 TRACKING · E
Arrows down: proceed only with evidence.
work-tracking · continuous

g.text: User story: “Add CSV export to the reports page.”
The developer supplies intent; E creates the work item.
Artifact: an open GitHub issue; its number is <n>.
"Add CSV export to the reports page" \
One unit of work, one item.
Frame the CSV-export question; split into 3–6 questions.
Fan out sub-agents; each returns sources + confidence.
Example questions: CSV behavior? Export approach?
Test coverage? Converge and reconcile contradictions.
Findings with citations, confidence, open questions,
Exit: resolve every open question or create a task.
Read the findings and relevant application code paths
yourself: the existing reports page and its tests.
Artifact: docs/plans/csv-export.md, with the work-item ID.
Example session-sized tasks: CSV generation; then
reports-page integration. Each has acceptance criteria,
a test approach, and an assigned tier.
Include goal/non-goals, context, test plan, risks with
owners/mitigations, and rollback. The plan stands alone.
Review against research: right problem, testable criteria,
rollback, and tasks finishable in one green session.
Record approval on the work item before code is written.
Rejected → revise the plan and seek approval again.
Read the approved plan fully; work in an isolated worktree.
Feature branch: gh-<n>-csv-export (one per work item).
Parallel executors never share a checkout.
Failing test → smallest change → refactor; task by task.
Complete one logical task per Conventional Commit;
stamp the work-item ID. Every commit builds and passes
Before handoff, use test-gate and also run:
Artifact: diff + green local gates + handoff note
(built, plan deltas, reasons, and what to probe).
Use an independent reviewer session; rerun in a clean
Audit skipped/pending/deleted tests; new behavior needs
a test that fails without the change. Read every changed line.
Review: plan conformance, tests, correctness, security,
maintainability, docs. Use the code-review skills.
Artifact: trimmed outputs, skip count, findings and verdict
on the work item; PR approval includes the work-item ID.
Both suites exit 0; no tests bypassed to obtain green.
Findings fixed or waived in writing by a human with reason.
RED → attach the failing case; fix, rerun, review again.
Scope/disputed findings → S revises plan → reapproval.
GREEN → approved evidence; merge may proceed.
Feature branch → PR → main (example default branch).
PR: what, why, tests, work-item ID, and risks to probe.
Only merge with green CI and reviewer approval.
Squash review fixups; each merged commit builds/tests.
Human merges in this example; artifact: the merged diff.
S prepares the version bump (consumer policy), changelog
and edited release notes with work-item IDs.
Annotated vX.Y.Z on merge commit; IDs in tag message.
Push tag. CI builds and attaches consumer artifacts.
Human always co-signs: presses publish or approves
the pipeline. Publish through the consumer’s channel.
Post-release: one concrete check from the outside
(install, endpoint, or smoke test); record the result.
Artifact: tagged release + notes + post-release evidence.
Include runtime rollback in the release notes.
Within a day, file follow-ups, review debt and new questions.
Artifact: a research backlog for the next delivery cycle.
Publishing ends by beginning research again.

svg.text: HOW TO READ THE RETURN ARROWS
Solid red: fix the failing case in 03. Dashed red: S revises 02, then reapprove.
Use systematic-debugging for failures; verify again until green. No self-approval.
Purple: publishing follow-ups seed 01. Tracker arrows: updates in the same session.
SOURCE MAP · paths relative to this repository
docs/workflows/README.md; 01-research.md; 02-planning.md; 03-execution.md;
04-verification.md; 05-tracking.md; 06-publishing.md (all under docs/workflows/)
docs/superpowers/README.md; docs/models/routing.md
docs/standards/git.md; docs/standards/testing.md; docs/standards/code-review.md
docs/integrations/README.md; docs/integrations/github.md
.agents/skills/{research-loop,planner-executor-handoff,test-gate,
work-tracking,release-publish}/SKILL.md (each card also has source metadata)
EXAMPLE CHOICES · not additional repository rules
GitHub; csv-export slug; illustrative research questions and task split; main; human merge.
Code analysis is part of planning. Branch finishing/merge is not an extra phase.
Human or second S can approve a plan; publishing always needs a human co-sign.
